W4.title: Supplied W4 English instructions — selected extract
W4.note: Verbatim selected English passages from canonical w04.json. Theme 4 restriction is from canonical w02.json, derived from the supplied theme workbook.

claims.title: Building types and boundaries
claims.explanation: The TKK reference lists slab, point, small apartment, row and detached types, and distinguishes plot, block and district floor-area ratios. New drawings are schematic. Equal floor area in different forms follows from summing the floor plates; it does not establish equal urban quality.

claims.title: Floor-area ratio
claims.explanation: e = sum of counted floor areas / selected land area. Illustrative equal-floor calculation: 1,000 × 4 / 5,000 = 0.80. Floor-count and land-area inputs are assumptions, not permissions or a regulatory definition of counted floor space.

claims.title: Model conversion
claims.explanation: A metre is 1,000 millimetres. At scale 1:n, model mm = real m × 1,000 / n. Thus 3.5 m at 1:500 is 7 mm. The initial scale is an example, not the workshop’s asserted scale. The paper/cardboard instruction is verbatim supplied English.

claims.title: Footway and clear widths
claims.explanation: Espoo: 2.5 m basic footway. SuRaKu card 1: 1.5 m clear passage, 1.8 m for two wheelchairs passing and 2.3 m for machine maintenance. Distinguish total route width from unobstructed passage.

claims.title: Cycling arrangements
claims.explanation: Espoo: shared route 3–4 m; separated walking/cycling total 4 m, main routes at least 4.5 m; one-way cycle lane 1.75 m, with a 0.75 m minimum extra buffer if adjacent to parking. These are different facility types; retain their context.

claims.title: Gradients, furniture and parking
claims.explanation: SuRaKu route crossfall: special/basic level 2%/3%; longitudinal gradient 5%/8%; ramps separate. Furniture belongs beside the route. Espoo 811A excludes cycle/scooter parking in the 5 m before a crossing, cycle crossing or intersecting cycle track. Capacity and handling space depend on layout.

claims.title: Wheelchair turning circles
claims.explanation: SuRaKu: clear turning diameter at least 1.5 m for a wheelchair, 2.5 m for a powered wheelchair. The sheet draws them at a common scale. Keep the usable envelope clear (editorial application of clear-space guidance); do not infer that every mobility scooter fits this envelope.

references.location: Card 3, PDF p. 5; also card 4 p. 7 and card 7 p. 13

claims.title: Passing and ramp landings
claims.explanation: SuRaKu: route clear width 1.5 m, passing 1.8 m. Ramp recommendation ≤5%, maximum 8%; on long ramps >5%, straight intermediate landings ≥2 m every 6 m. The separate ramp width and turn details remain in the source. Example: run = rise / gradient = 0.30/0.05 = 6 m, excluding landings.

references.location: Cards 1–3; ramp profile and text on PDF pp. 5–6

claims.title: Seating and accessible parking
claims.explanation: SuRaKu: wheelchair space ≥0.9 m at a bench end; backs, armrests and varied seat heights. Courtyard accessible bay ≥3.6 × 5 m, gradient ≤2% both directions. Kerbside bays and vehicle transfer/lift access need separate layouts. The sentence about joining shared spaces is an editorial design prompt.

claims.title: Tram corridors and bus-stop lengths
claims.explanation: Espoo light-rail reservation ≥8 m, stops separately; Helsinki’s draft tram card gives ≥6 m on a line section. They are not the same reservation. Espoo 031D gives 16 m for one bus, 32 m for two, using a 15 m bus; additional approach, junction and crossing clearances are shown separately.

references.location: Periaateratkaisu ja mitoitus; source marked draft

claims.title: Local collector and essential vehicle functions
claims.explanation: Espoo local-collector lane 3.0–3.25 m; when buses govern, ≥3.25 m. Turning depends on the vehicle and junction. The W4 brief lists servicing, deliveries, waste collection and rescue access, and excludes long-term private-car parking. Turning sketch is illustrative, not a computed path.

claims.title: Rescue geometry
claims.explanation: HIKLU: fire engine and aerial appliance route width 3.5 m, clear height 4.2 m. Inner/outer radii: engine 5/10.5 m; aerial 5.5/12.5 m. Aerial set-up width ≥6 m, target 8 m, length 13 m. The vehicle models also specify driving allowance 0.4 m and aerial boom allowance 1.0 m. Our circles do not add these allowances or simulate a manoeuvre. Check loads, slopes, reach, trees, wires and snow against the complete guide.

claims.title: Tree soil volume
claims.explanation: Helsinki’s draft tree-and-tram card gives approximately 25 m³ conventional soil for a large-growing tree and discusses 40–60 m³ structural soil because stone displaces water storage. These are contextual indicative volumes, not a universal minimum. Coordinate roots, utilities and mature crown; grouped trees should have continuous soil.

references.location: Puiden kasvualustan mitoitus; source marked draft

claims.title: Detention example
claims.explanation: Espoo’s Kaavoitus section gives an example zoning provision: 1 m³ per 100 m² impermeable surface, emptying in 12–24 h and controlled overflow. It is not asserted for this site. Example calculation: 600/100 = 6 m³; at assumed 0.20 m effective depth, 6/0.20 = 30 m² idealised plan area. Side slopes, freeboard, ground conditions and actual inflow/outflow are not calculated.

claims.title: Planting strips and shared ground
claims.explanation: Espoo planting widths: trees ≥3 m (main streets ≥3.5 m); lawn/ground cover ≥2 m. These do not prove adequate soil volume. The checks for utilities, snow, sightlines, overhead wires and salt are a synthesis of the listed guides.

claims.title: Width budget and strip templates
claims.explanation: Total = Σ(width × count); remainder = available − total. Default: 2×2.5 + 2×1.75 + 2×3 + 2×3.25 = 21 m, leaving 3 m of an assumed 24 m street. Optional tram uses 8 m. The combination, street width, strip lengths and zero initial buffer are editorial assumptions; this is arithmetic, not a validated cross-section. The CAD export treats all rows as separate adjacent strips and makes no sharing allowance.

references.location: Separate needs must be negotiated in the shared model

claims.title: Checks beyond the sum
claims.explanation: Editorial synthesis: a cross-section sum does not establish junction operation, loading space, accessible continuity, below-ground compatibility, canopy clearance or a rescue arrangement. Check sections, plans and vertical envelopes together. Shared use must be justified rather than subtracted automatically.

claims.title: Shared-model discussion
claims.explanation: The questions and closing statements on the sheet are verbatim selected English W4 passages. The course sources remain authoritative. This helper adds no deadline, submission, assessment or allocation rule.

claims.title: CAD units, templates and limits
claims.explanation: All canonical geometry is stored in metres. DXF coordinates are multiplied by 1 for metres, 1,000 for millimetres or 1/0.3048 for international feet. DXF $INSUNITS is respectively 6, 4 or 2. Files use R2000 DXF. Coordinates and text are rounded to four decimals in the selected unit. SVG is a vector preview with user units matching the selection, not a physical-size print template. The evidence above is the proof for geometry; exact conversion does not make the source values more precise.
